text: A surgeon cut three tiny holes in a man's knee, splashed some water around, and stuck on three plasters. He never once went inside the knee. The nurse leans in and whispers, Doctor, you forgot the operation. Back in the 1990s in Houston, surgeons scrape and rinse sore knees all day long. Then another doctor asks him a nasty question. What if it's all in their heads, so he takes 180 sore knees and splits them into three groups. 60 get scraped, 60 get rinsed, and 60 get the trick. Everyone signs a form saying they might get a pretend surgery and nobody is told which. For the trick, a real operation plays on the screen. He wiggles the leg and splashes water loudly so it sounds real. Two years later, the man from the table is climbing stairs again, pain way down, and the real surgery groups know better at all. Three pain charts, all the same height. You see, the work inside the knee wasn't what made them feel better. Being sure you're fixed can make a knee hurt less, like a kid in the waiting room. A nurse plasters his scraped knee and it stops hurting. In 2004, Medicare stopped paying for it, for arthritis knee pain. Turns out the nurse was right. He forgot the operation and the patients never missed it.
